incident-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT: Elevated 95th/99th tail latency for /v1/generate in us-west-2. Error spike correlated with KV cache miss rate rising from 2% -> 23% since 05:14 UTC. Paging oncall@sre.

sara (oncall): I'm paged, looking now. can someone share customer impact?

dan (runtime): we're seeing a hot prefix pattern — lots of short prefixed contexts causing eviction churn on the prefix/KV cache. downstream requests falling back to full model runs which bumps tail latency.

maria (sre): support metrics: ~14 customers reported error 503s in last 10m, overall p95 latency up from 120ms -> 980ms. No CPU/GPU OOMs. network ok.

kevin (support): we have one enterprise customer with high QPS hitting it hard, they're seeing timeouts. Customer notified (case #14922).

sara (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) apply short-term traffic shaping to the offending tenant(s) 2) temporarily bypass prefix cache for correctness-sensitive routes 3) tighten per-tenant rate limits for heavy prefixes 4) coordinate handoff if this goes >30m.

dan (runtime): agree. I'm ready to flip a bypass flag for prefix lookup on the runtime. note: bypass increases cost but avoids stale/incorrect cache returns.

ops-bot: rolling change queued: route-control/update -> apply traffic-shaping policy (change id: ts-188412).

maria (sre): sara — can you run per-tenant rate cap for the heavy tenant now? suggest soft cap from 1.2k rps -> 400 rps with 10s burst.

sara (oncall): applying soft cap to tenant:acme-inc now.

support-bot: ACTION: applied tenant rate limit: tenant=acme-inc new_limit=400rps burst=10s applied_by=sara ts=1884123489

kevin (support): confirmed reduced retry storms from that tenant, request rate to the kv cluster dropped ~60% in 30s. Customer still seeing some errors but fewer.

maria (sre): next: enable prefix-KV bypass for correctness-sensitive reads on the path that does prefix resolution only. dan, can you push the bypass flag to the runtime group canary=10%?

dan (runtime): pushing flag to canary nodes now. command:```curl -XPOST https://runtime-admin/api/flags -d '{"flag":"prefix_kv_bypass","value":true,"canary_pct":10}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN'``` will watch logs.

ops-bot: flag rollout started -> prefix_kv_bypass canary=10% (op id: op-1884123498).

maria (sre): observed canary behaviour: bypass reduces kv read latency but increases token compute by ~8% on those nodes. p95 latency for canary nodes improved ~200ms.

sara (oncall): ramp bypass to 50% if no regressions in 5m.

incident-bot: NOTE: escalation timer set 00:30:00 from 1884123456.

dan (runtime): ramping to 50% now.```

curl -XPOST https://runtime-admin/api/flags -d '{"flag":"prefix_kv_bypass","value":true,"canary_pct":50}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN'```

ops-bot: rollout in progress -> prefix_kv_bypass canary=50% (op id: op-1884123524).

maria (sre): after ramp to 50%: cluster-level p95 dropped from 980ms -> 420ms. kv miss-rate still elevated but fewer fallbacks.

sara (oncall): good. next short-term: add temporary request-level rate limiting on /v1/generate for anonymous/unknown API keys to 5rps to reduce noisy unknown traffic. dan/maria can you validate no auth regressions?

dan (runtime): will validate. applying rule in WAF:```policy add name=anon-gen-rate limit=5rps path=/v1/generate```

ops-bot: WAF policy applied id=waf-1884123600.

kevin (support): Customer update: acme-inc sees p50 normal, p95 improved, still occasional 504s but reduced. They've paused heavy batch jobs.

maria (sre): monitoring: CPU/GPU spend increased ~6% due to bypass but within committed capacity. cost delta acceptable for correctness. recommend keeping bypass + tenant caps for now.

sara (oncall): OK keep measures. set follow-up tasks: - postmortem - root cause triage (hot prefix detection/improved shielding) - improve auto-burst shielding for tenants hitting hot prefixes. I'll handoff to dan for long-term runtime fix in 1 hour.

dan (runtime): accepting handoff. planned next steps: 1) debug eviction churn metrics, 2) add adaptive prefix sharding and per-prefix token buckets, 3) tweak cache eviction policy to be TTL-aware for short contexts.

incident-bot: HANDOFF: oncall_from=sara to=dan at=1884123710 reason="long-term remediation"

sara (oncall): leaving a note: mitigation state=active, bypass=true(50%), tenant caps=acme-inc 400rps, anon-gen 5rps, estimated time-to-stable 45m.

kevin (support): I'll keep customer comms open, will escalate if they see regression.

maria (sre): timeline: continue to monitor for 30m. if p95 > 600ms escalate to incident lead.

dan (runtime): capturing logs and a snapshot of eviction counters:```EVICT_COUNTS: prefix_evictions=124k last_5m=78k
KV_MISS_RATE: 22.7%
CACHE_HOT_PREFIXES: ["/ctx/0x9a...", "/ctx/0x4f..."]
BUCKET_STATS: tenant=acme-inc tokens=95% used
```

incident-bot: SUMMARY at 1884123800: mitigations applied: tenant rate cap, anon rate limit, prefix_kv_bypass rolled to 50%. Early results: p95 improved ~56%, customer impact reduced. Postmortem owner=dan; timeline target=1884127200. :white_check_mark:

sara (oncall): thanks team. leaving channel, ping if anything spikes. :raised_hands:

kevin (support): noted, will update customer after 30m window.

maria (sre): filing initial incident stub: INC-188412 (title omitted per policy). assigning to dan for RCA and to infra for mitigation improvements.

dan (runtime): on it. I'll post follow-up with root cause and recommended code changes.

support-bot: THREAD CLOSED temporarily for triage. React :lock: to re-open.
